What to look for in waterproof gloves

  • Knuckle and palm protection. Look for hard or moulded knuckle armour and palm sliders that resist abrasion.
  • Waterproofing. A membrane like Gore-Tex or Drystar keeps hands dry — vital for safe control in UK rain.
  • Fit and feel. Gloves should be snug with no loose fingertips so you keep full control of the levers.
  • Season-specific. Vented summer gloves and insulated winter gloves do very different jobs — many tourers own both.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on waterproof gloves?

Our catalogue spans £54.99 to £239.95. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Held, Rev'it, Klim, Spidi, Alpinestars. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.q: Do waterproof gloves stay dry in heavy rain?
faq.a: A membrane glove keeps water out well, but water can still track down your sleeve and in through the cuff on long wet rides. Wear the cuff under a sealed jacket gauntlet, or choose a gauntlet glove worn over the sleeve, to stop that.

faq.q: Gore-Tex or Drystar, which is better?
faq.a: Both work. Gore-Tex, used on the Held Air N Dry II and Rev'it Dominator 3, is the benchmark for breathable waterproofing. Alpinestars Drystar, on the S Max and SP X Z, performs nearly as well for less money. Pick on fit and budget.

faq.q: Are waterproof gloves warm enough for winter?
faq.a: Most waterproof gloves are three-season and only lightly insulated. For genuine cold, below about 5C, choose a dedicated winter or heated glove instead. A waterproof glove keeps you dry but will not keep fingers warm on frosty mornings.

faq.q: How do I care for waterproof gloves?
faq.a: Rinse off road salt and grime, then air dry away from direct heat, which can crack leather and damage the membrane. Reproof the outer leather with a suitable wax or spray so water beads rather than soaking in and chilling your hands.
